_note: Optional catalog read by the /plugins command. Add entries here to extend the catalog — no code changes needed elsewhere. Re-run the installer after editing to sync.

catalog.name: Playwright MCP
catalog.summary: Drives a real browser via natural language, using the accessibility tree (no vision model, no screenshots). Good for validating UI changes end-to-end.
catalog.recommend_if: package.json depends on react/vue/svelte/next/nuxt/angular, or the project has an index.html / vite.config / webpack.config — i.e. it has a frontend to click through.

catalog.name: Supabase MCP
catalog.summary: Lets the agent manage tables, run SQL, and read project config directly against a Supabase project.
catalog.recommend_if: package.json/requirements has a supabase dependency, or a supabase/ folder with config.toml exists.
requires_input: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN (personal access token, from the Supabase dashboard)

catalog.name: Postgres MCP
catalog.summary: Query and inspect a local/remote Postgres database directly from the agent.
catalog.recommend_if: package.json/requirements has pg/psycopg/prisma-with-postgres, or a DATABASE_URL pointing at postgres:// is set in .env.

catalog.name: SQLite MCP
catalog.summary: Query and inspect a local SQLite database file directly from the agent.
catalog.recommend_if: A .sqlite/.db file exists in the project, or package.json depends on better-sqlite3/sqlite3.

catalog.name: Strix
catalog.summary: Autonomous AI pentest agent — explores, exploits, and proves vulnerabilities with working PoCs instead of a static scan list. Runs sandboxed in Docker. Used by /audit when installed.
catalog.recommend_if: The project handles auth, payments, or user data, or the user wants deeper coverage than npm audit / gitleaks for /audit.

catalog.name: Skill UI bundle (frontend-design + baseline-ui)
catalog.summary: Design-quality skills: /frontend-design generates a real design direction instead of a generic template, /baseline-ui strips 'agent UI slop' (spacing, typography, states), /fixing-accessibility covers keyboard/labels/focus.
catalog.recommend_if: The project has a UI you're actively designing (frontend framework detected, or the user is asking for visual/design work).

catalog.name: MCP Builder (Anthropic official)
catalog.summary: Structured 4-phase guide (research, implementation, review, evaluation) for building high-quality MCP servers, with language-specific guidance for TypeScript and Python.
catalog.recommend_if: You need to build a custom MCP server (no ready-made one covers the API/service you need) instead of just consuming one of the servers base_project already registers.

catalog.name: Webapp Testing (Anthropic official)
catalog.summary: Playwright-based toolkit for testing local web apps: UI functionality checks, screenshots, console log capture, and a decision tree for static vs dynamic testing. Complements the Playwright MCP already in this catalog.
catalog.recommend_if: The project has a frontend you want automated end-to-end checks on, beyond what the Playwright MCP alone gives you.

catalog.name: Headroom
catalog.summary: Context-compression layer: shrinks tool outputs, logs, and JSON before they hit the model. Reports ~20% fewer tokens for coding agents, 60-95% for JSON responses — reinforces base_project's own token-economy rules.
catalog.recommend_if: Universal — helps on any project, most on ones with noisy tool output (large JSON APIs, verbose logs, big files).

catalog.name: CodeBurn
catalog.summary: Local dashboard for AI coding token/cost usage across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and opencode. No API key, reads local session data. Run on demand, no persistent install needed.
catalog.recommend_if: Universal — anyone who wants visibility into what their AI coding sessions actually cost.

install.note: runs on demand, nothing to install persistently

catalog.name: Ruflo
catalog.summary: Multi-agent orchestration meta-harness: ~98 specialized agents, swarm topologies (mesh/hierarchical/adaptive), and persistent HNSW vector memory that learns from past coordination. Heavier than everything else in this catalog — it's infrastructure, not a single skill.
catalog.recommend_if: You regularly parallelize real dev work across many agents (multi-service refactors, large migrations) and want persistent cross-session memory, not just base_project's built-in architect/coder/reviewer trio.
requires_input: Review resource/cost implications before installing — it registers its own MCP server and maintains its own vector DB.

claude.instruction: claude mcp add ruflo -- npx ruflo@latest mcp start

opencode.note: Ruflo's opencode support is less mature than its Claude Code integration — verify before relying on it.

catalog.name: Ponytail
catalog.summary: Injects a 'laziest senior dev' discipline: prefers the zero-code / standard-library solution over writing new code. Independently reported to cut ~54% of code volume in tests. Overlaps in spirit with base_project's own coder agent — treat as reinforcement, not replacement.
catalog.recommend_if: Universal, opt-in for anyone who wants a stronger anti-overengineering bias than the default coder agent already provides.

opencode.note: lands in ~/.agents/skills/ — also copy the ponytail* folders into ~/.config/opencode/skills/ afterward so opencode (which reads skills from its own confirmed skills/ dir) definitely picks them up. The 'opencode-ponytail' npm package is deprecated, do not use it.
